answer: Identity is quarried, not minted. Each operator's quarry is public, and a new identity must draw from a site certified by a karst survey measuring how long the rock has held, so a fresh canyon certifies nothing until it ages. Because certification is issued per site rather than per identity, all accounts cut from one quarry share one rating, so n aliases never multiply standing. The k-th survey an operator commissions costs k squared, so crowding a canyon grows the bill cubically, and each walnut seal that certifies a site is non-transferable, so it cannot be bought, rented, or lent to a farm.
